headline: Youth development recruitment exam postponed over question leak
summary: Candidates staged protests and blocked roads across Dhaka after the exam for 242 posts was cancelled on the day of the test.
details: The recruitment exam for assistant Upazila youth development officers was postponed following allegations that the question paper had been leaked.
The exam for 242 posts in the 11th pay grade was scheduled to take place at nearly 100 centres across the capital.
Allegations of the leak began circulating on social media on Friday night, leading to the postponement announcement on Saturday.
Many candidates arrived at their centres on Saturday morning only to find the test had been postponed, sparking protests.
Demonstrations broke out at several locations, including Mirpur, Manik Mia Avenue, Nilkhet, and Motijheel.
Protesters blocked Manik Mia Avenue and gathered outside the Department of Youth Development headquarters in Dilkusha, Motijheel.
The protests caused significant traffic congestion on several major roads across Dhaka.
Police reported that the road blockade at Manik Mia Avenue was cleared about an hour later.
caption:
Exam postponed on the day of the test! Job seekers block roads in Dhaka after question paper leak allegations.

The recruitment exam for assistant Upazila youth development officers was postponed following allegations that the question paper had been leaked.

The exam for 242 posts in the 11th pay grade was scheduled to take place at nearly 100 centres across the capital.

Allegations of the leak began circulating on social media on Friday night, leading to the postponement announcement on Saturday.

Many candidates arrived at their centres on Saturday morning only to find the test had been postponed, sparking protests.

Demonstrations broke out at several locations, including Mirpur, Manik Mia Avenue, Nilkhet, and Motijheel.

Protesters blocked Manik Mia Avenue and gathered outside the Department of Youth Development headquarters in Dilkusha, Motijheel.

The protests caused significant traffic congestion on several major roads across Dhaka.

Police reported that the road blockade at Manik Mia Avenue was cleared about an hour later.

headline: Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee and others detained in Delhi protests
summary: Opposition leaders and activists were taken into custody while attempting to march against the Election Commission amid heavy security.
details: Delhi Police detained several high-profile figures, including AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal and West Bengal's Mamata Banerjee, during protests against the Election Commission.
The crackdown included the detention of former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan, activists Neha Bora and Yogendra Yadav, and lawyer Prashant Bhushan.
Police blocked demonstrators from reaching Jantar Mantar, with reports that Kejriwal was dragged away by personnel while attempting to reach the protest site.
Arvind Kejriwal accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of running a dictatorship and alleged that the recent election was won through vote manipulation.
In a social media post, Kejriwal described the current state of the country as worse than the Emergency, claiming the government is suppressing democracy.
He further called for the removal of both Prime Minister Modi and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alleging electoral fraud.
caption:
Opposition leaders detained in Delhi as protests intensify against the Election Commission.

Delhi Police detained several high-profile figures, including AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal and West Bengal's Mamata Banerjee, during protests against the Election Commission.

The crackdown included the detention of former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan, activists Neha Bora and Yogendra Yadav, and lawyer Prashant Bhushan.

Police blocked demonstrators from reaching Jantar Mantar, with reports that Kejriwal was dragged away by personnel while attempting to reach the protest site.

Arvind Kejriwal accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of running a dictatorship and alleged that the recent election was won through vote manipulation.

In a social media post, Kejriwal described the current state of the country as worse than the Emergency, claiming the government is suppressing democracy.

He further called for the removal of both Prime Minister Modi and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alleging electoral fraud.
